prs.title: fix(shared): make UrlElicitationRequiredError pickle-safe (refs #2431)
prs.author: MukundaKatta
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug: MCPError (specifically UrlElicitationRequiredError) is not pickle-safe. The default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but self.args is set to (code, message, data) by MCPError.__init__ while UrlElicitationRequiredError's constructor signature is (elicitations, message=None) — causing a TypeError on every unpickle. This is tracked as issue #2431. #2478 takes a generic approach (a module-level _restore_mcp_error() helper meant to reconstruct any MCPError subclass via from_error_data(), special-casing UrlElicitationRequiredError via from_error()), while #2555 fixes it locally by adding __reduce__ directly on UrlElicitationRequiredError, reconstructing from (self._elicitations, self.message). (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: #2555 ships a complete, verifiable fix: it adds tests/shared/test_exceptions.py coverage for the pickle round-trip and its diff shows the actual __reduce__ call site wired into the class. #2478's diff only introduces the _restore_mcp_error() helper and strips a '# pragma: no cover' from MCPError.data, but the shown diff never shows the helper being called anywhere (no __reduce__ addition/modification) and includes no test changes — so the fix isn't demonstrated to actually run, and the coverage-pragma removal isn't backed by a visible new test. members.title: fix(shared): preserve MCPError payload on pickle
members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2555: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug: MCPError (specifically UrlElicitationRequiredError) is not pickle-safe. The default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but self.args is set to (code, message, data) by MCPError.__init__ while UrlElicitationRequiredError's constructor signature is (elicitations, message=None) — causing a TypeError on every unpickle. This is tracked as issue #2431. #2478 takes a generic approach (a module-level _restore_mcp_error() helper meant to reconstruct any MCPError subclass via from_error_data(), special-casing UrlElicitationRequiredError via from_error()), while #2555 fixes it locally by adding __reduce__ directly on UrlElicitationRequiredError, reconstructing from (self._elicitations, self.message).

clusters.pick_reason: #2493 only deletes the offending 'send an error response' call, covering solely the case where the peer already sent notifications/cancelled (message.cancelled). #2514 goes further: it imports CancelledNotificationParams to actively emit a spec-compliant notifications/cancelled notification, covering the additional cases named in its title (request timeout and caller-side cancellation) where the peer would otherwise never learn the request was abandoned. #2514 also removes a `# pragma: no cover` marker on the adjacent guard clause, indicating it adds test coverage for a previously-untested branch, whereas #2493's diff includes no test changes. #2514's fix is a strict superset of #2493's change location and intent, so keeping it and closing #2493 avoids losing the timeout/caller-cancellation handling.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: Both rewrite the same block in RequestResponder.cancel() in src/mcp/shared/session.py — the code right after `self._cancel_scope.cancel(); self._completed = True` — which currently sends an error response to indicate cancellation, violating the MCP/JSON-RPC spec requirement that a receiver must not send a response for a cancelled request. members.title: fix(shared): preserve MCPError payload on pickle
members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2555: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug: MCPError (specifically UrlElicitationRequiredError) is not pickle-safe. The default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but self.args is set to (code, message, data) by MCPError.__init__ while UrlElicitationRequiredError's constructor signature is (elicitations, message=None) — causing a TypeError on every unpickle. This is tracked as issue #2431. #2478 takes a generic approach (a module-level _restore_mcp_error() helper meant to reconstruct any MCPError subclass via from_error_data(), special-casing UrlElicitationRequiredError via from_error()), while #2555 fixes it locally by adding __reduce__ directly on UrlElicitationRequiredError, reconstructing from (self._elicitations, self.message).
